newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady in lacklustre trade, with most traders waiting for the outcome of U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony before the Senate Finance Committee today, dealers said on Thursday.
"Everyone is waiting for the outcome of Greenspan's speech tonight. We will be watching his speech closely for fresh clues on inflation," a local dealer said.
The market is also waiting for today's issue of the U.S. weekly jobless claims figures.
Weekly jobless claims for the week ending January 25, are forecast to be around 348,000 compared with 355,000 reported in the previous week.
"Alan Greenspan's speech will probably overshadow tonight's weekly jobless claims figures, as everyone is waiting for more clues to market direction from his speech," another dealer said.

"Some people are also waiting for possible direction from this Friday's release of the (U.S. January) Chicago purchasing managers index and next week's Federal Open Market Committee meeting," he said.
In day-to-day rates, Thursday/Friday and weekend eased 1/16 percentage point each to a common 5-7/16 5-5/16 percent, respectively.
Week-fixed was unchanged from Wednesday's 5-7/16 5-5/16 percent.

Among longer dates, two-months rose 1/8 point to 5-9/16 5-7/16 percent, four-months unchanged at 5-9/16 5-7/16, six-months unchanged at 5-11/16 5-9/16 and twelve-months unchanged at 5-15/16 5-13/16 percent.
